record.original_question: How many bits of precision are necessary to guarantee that CG applied to an $n$ by $n$ SPD linear system $Ax=b$ obtains an approximate solution with normwise backward error at most $epsilon$ in $n$ (or fewer) steps?

evidence.quote: How many bits of precision are necessary to guarantee that CG applied to an $n$ by $n$ SPD linear system $Ax=b$ obtains an approximate solution with normwise backward error at most $\epsilon$ in $n$ (or fewer) steps?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be a symmetric positive definite matrix and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Consider the conjugate gradient (CG) method applied to the linear system $Ax = b$, implemented in finite-precision floating-point arithmetic with $t$ bits of precision (unit roundoff $u = 2^{-t}$). Given a tolerance $\varepsilon > 0$, an approximate solution $\tilde{x}$ is said to have normwise backward error at most $\varepsilon$ if there exist a perturbation matrix $\Delta A$ and a perturbation vector $\Delta b$ with
$$\|\Delta A\| \le \varepsilon \|A\|, \qquad \|\Delta b\| \le \varepsilon \|b\|,$$
such that $(A + \Delta A)\tilde{x} = b + \Delta b$ (in some fixed norm, e.g. the 2-norm).

Determine the minimum number of bits of precision $t = t(n,\varepsilon, A, b)$ that suffices to guarantee that CG, run on $A$ and $b$ in floating-point arithmetic with precision $t$, produces in at most $n$ iterations an approximate solution whose normwise backward error is at most $\varepsilon$. Equivalently, find sharp upper and lower bounds on the precision required, as a function of $n$, $\varepsilon$, and (possibly) properties of $A$ such as the condition number $\kappa(A)$, that ensure CG terminates within $n$ steps with normwise backward error $\le \varepsilon$.
artifact.category_tag: Numerical linear algebra / finite-precision conjugate gradient
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (e.g., 2024–2025 analyses of finite-precision and mixed-precision (preconditioned) CG) provide partial backward-error bounds of the form $O(u)\kappa(A)^{1/2}$ under various assumptions, but a sharp characterization of the number of bits of precision needed so that CG attains normwise backward error $\le \varepsilon$ within $n$ steps for any SPD system is not established. The question of necessary/sufficient precision for CG to converge in at most $n$ steps to a given backward-error level appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Forward and backward error bounds for a mixed precision preconditioned conjugate gradient algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Under reasonable assumptions, the framework can produce a backward error bounded by the unit roundoff times a polynomial in the dimension; relative backward and forward errors of PCG can reach O(u)κ(A)^{1/2}.
status_evidence.claim: Recent analyses give partial backward-error bounds for CG/PCG in finite precision but do not pin down the precise number of bits required for n-step convergence to error ε.

status_evidence.title: On the Convergence Rate of Variants of the Conjugate Gradient Algorithm in Finite Precision Arithmetic
status_evidence.snippet: Studies convergence behavior of CG variants in finite precision; precise precision requirements for guaranteed n-step backward error remain a topic of active investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Precision requirements for guaranteed termination of CG within n steps at a prescribed backward-error level are still being investigated.
